Unaffected relatives tested: not reported. Note the papers overlap, so these are not independent families.

concerns: Same people reported repeatedly; the pipeline kept 19 identities. Likely matches (panel to confirm): 31384100 P1 = 36211342 #5 = 40574834 P4 (onset 6 months; 40574834 cites Hori, its ref 10, for P4); 31384100 P2 (mother) = 36211342 #6 = 40574834 P6 (Crohn's disease, Hashimoto's); 31384100 P3 (grandmother) = 36211342 #7 = 40574834 P7 (stomatitis from early childhood, Hashimoto's); 31384100 P4 (uncle, Hodgkin's lymphoma and craniopharyngioma) = 39845949 case 11 = 40574834 P8; 39845949 case 12 = 40574834 P10 (female, onset 2 months, aseptic meningitis), possibly also 31384100 P6 or P7; 31384100 P5 (fever from 1 yr, HT) may be 40574834 P9 (onset 1 yr, Hashimoto's). 40574834 P5 is unmatched. Count the family once for segregation.
Transcript: 31384100 states NM_006290.2, not the batch transcript NM_001270508.2; the c. position is the same string (c.2209delC).
31384100 says the variant was in 'all the HT members tested' in one place and 'all members tested' in another; which members were genotyped is shown only in Fig. 2, not in the text.
39845949 counts case 11's craniopharyngioma as CNS involvement of HA20; 31384100 also reports Hodgkin's lymphoma in the same man. Both are unusual features the panel may weigh.
Functional evidence is cited from a prior paper (Kadowaki et al. 2018) that is not in this batch.
A shared HLA haplotype is present in the HT members (31384100), a possible other genetic contributor to the thyroid phenotype as the authors note.
notes_for_panel: Large single family with co-segregation of the variant with an autoinflammatory/autoimmune phenotype across three generations, reported in four overlapping papers. Unaffected tested relatives are not reported, so segregation counts rest on affected carriers only.
